description: Compiled runtime-facing models and canonical input requirements for GPT Pro repaired tax-gap candidates. Customer-facing totals remain off by default until each rule has complete user/tax-document inputs and explicit inclusion policy.

notes: These records do not make tax estimates customer-facing by themselves.
Sales/use exemptions and state credits calculate only after required tax profile, invoice, certificate, filing, and liability inputs are present.
Local business-tax and gross-receipts rows are compiled into local tax workflows where the current runtime supports the formula shape.
Property-tax credits, exemptions, special valuations, and abatements remain tax-bill, assessor, or program-document gates.

ALDOR forms confirm Form CO:CAA and ST:EX-A2 workflow, and the official ruling page warns that a revenue ruling is limited to its facts and taxpayer. ([Alabama Department of Revenue][2])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote only as a Chapter 9B project-specific abatement workflow. The skipped record should not be modeled as a general retrofit sales/use exemption, because the official sources require granting-authority approval, ALDOR documentation, a project certificate, and itemized qualifying project purchases.

Official fiscal notes show sales/use abatement calculated on eligible purchases by applying the combined rate less the Local School Support Tax component in the reviewed Clark County example. rules.evidenceText: New Mexico TRD describes New Mexico as imposing gross receipts tax on persons engaged in business rather than a conventional retail sales tax. TRD Form RPD-41341 states that, effective July 1, 2007, a deduction from gross receipts tax is available for the sale and installation of a solar energy system. New Mexico 2021 SB0243 amended Section 7-9-112 to provide that, prior to July 1, 2030, receipts from the sale and installation of solar energy systems may be deducted from gross receipts.
rules.reasoningNotes: Reviewed the uploaded repair prompt and target constraints before official-source research.  Promote only the source-backed solar-energy-system gross receipts deduction into the gross_receipts_or_bo_rate_preference model. Do not model a broad clean-energy or retrofit sales/use tax exemption for New Mexico because no current official broad retrofit-specific rule was identified in the official sources reviewed. Customer-facing savings remains gated because the deduction is claimed by the seller or installer and any customer benefit depends on transaction pricing, pass-through treatment, rate, and filing confirmation.

rules.evidenceText: Arizona DOR states that the renewable energy production tax credit applies to individual and corporate income taxpayers that own a qualified energy generator first producing electricity before January 1, 2021, requires ADOR approval and certification, is not residential, and is subject to a $20,000,000 annual aggregate cap. A.R.S. Sections 43-1083.02 and 43-1164.03 provide the ten-year credit period, resource-specific production rates, $2,000,000 facility annual cap, $20,000,000 annual aggregate cap, first-come certification process, co-owner allocation, and five-year carryforward. ADOR program guidelines state that first production after 2020 is not eligible and that the final application year is 2030.
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote as a legacy/current certificate workflow, not as a new residential clean-energy credit. Runtime status remains needs_filing_confirmation because RetroFi cannot compute customer-facing savings from production estimates alone; ADOR certification, annual cap position, production-year number, qualified-resource classification, and taxpayer-level credit/carryforward data are required.

rules.evidenceText: Colorado DOR states that the prior heat pump system income tax credit and sales tax exemption expired December 31, 2023, and that beginning January 1, 2024 the new heat pump tax credit is available only to a heat pump tax credit contractor registered with the Colorado Energy Office. DOR DR1322 for 2025 states that the contractor must provide a discount separately stated on the receipt or invoice, that building owners generally cannot claim the credit unless they are registered contractors installing their own heat pump, and that 2025 credit amounts are $500 for heat pump water heaters, $1,500 for air-source or variable refrigerant flow heat pumps, and $3,000 for ground-source, water-source, or combined-source heat pumps. Colorado Revised Statutes Section 39-22-554 provides the 2024-2032 technology-specific amount schedule and unit-count rules. HB26-1289 amended the statutory revenue-forecast reduction provisions and related program administration provisions.
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote because the official statute and DOR form provide a modelable heat pump contractor income tax credit with technology-specific amounts and unit-count rules. Keep customer-facing calculation gated because the credit belongs to the registered contractor, the customer benefit depends on a separately stated invoice discount and current CEO/DOR discount mechanics, and current-year form treatment or statutory forecast reduction may change the allowed amount.

rules.evidenceText: Prince George's County states the Green Business credit applies to the county portion of tax on qualifying real or personal property for up to five consecutive years, is first-come and subject to funding, requires third-party certification and an October 1 filing, may not be stacked with another local or state property tax credit for the same property, and must be passed through when an eligible lessee is contractually liable for the taxes. The County application supplies the operational percentages: Green Business real property 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% for years 1-5, and Green Business personal property 50% for years 1-5. County high-performance materials supply the new-or-major renovation rates of 25%, 50%, and 75% for 5 years and existing-building O+M rates of 10%, 25%, and 50% for 3 years, with October 1 filing and a $5,000,000 fiscal-year aggregate cap. ([Prince George's County Government][1])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote because the county pages, county applications, county bills, and Maryland enabling statutes provide amount, duration, caps, filing conditions, and anti-stacking rules. rules.evidenceText: RPTL §487 exempts eligible energy systems from taxation to the extent of the increase in assessed value attributable to the system for 15 years, requires owner application on the prescribed form by taxable status date, allows local opt-out by counties, cities, towns, villages, and school districts by technology category, and allows solar or wind PILOT treatment in non-opt-out jurisdictions. The Tax Department publishes an official list of filed local laws and resolutions, with the reviewed list showing records on file as of March 31, 2026. Form RP-487 and its instructions provide the assessor-facing incremental-cost calculation and filing workflow. ([NY Tax Department][3])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote as a safe assessor/PILOT workflow rather than a deterministic statewide savings calculator. The statutory formula is source-backed, but parcel-level savings depend on assessor-approved exempt assessed value, overlapping taxing jurisdictions, opt-out status, PILOT status, and current tax rates.

rules.evidenceText: Virginia Code §58.1-3661 provides that certified solar equipment may be wholly or partially exempted by local ordinance, requires local building-department certification after application, requires assessor valuation, and applies the exemption for a term not less than 5 years; the same statute separately treats qualifying systems of 25 kW or less installed under §15.2-2288.7(A) or (B) as wholly exempt from state and local taxation. The Virginia Administrative Code supplies application, certification, and valuation procedures and component valuation rules. Alexandria official materials provide a 5-year solar equipment exemption and an example using 100% of cost and installation for solar panels/hot-water equipment. City of Fairfax official materials provide a 10-year program effective for qualifying installations on or after January 1, 2022, with Code Administration certification and Real Estate Assessment Office valuation. Richmond and Virginia Beach official sources checked did not supply a complete current local-option solar exemption row with ordinance, application workflow, exemption percent, and term for promotion. ([Virginia Law][4])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote only the verified Alexandria and City of Fairfax locality subrules within this broader Virginia follow-up. Keep all other Virginia localities, including Richmond and Virginia Beach based on the official sources checked here, behind a document/local-ordinance gate until exact official local adoption, certification, exemption percentage, eligible system definition, and assessor workflow are available.

rules.evidenceText: MEDC's RERZ fact sheet states that benefits apply only to operations of the designated company within approved geographic boundaries, identifies the local resolution and MSF/SAB approval workflow, lists taxes not paid and taxes still due, requires tax-current status, and states that approved companies enter MSF agreements; it also states taxes can be abated up to 15 years and relief is phased out in 25% increments over the last three years. ([MEDC][7]) MEDC's Michigan Strategic Fund page states that the MSF Board recommends Agricultural Processing, Renewable Energy, and Forest Products Processing Renaissance Zone designations to the State Administrative Board. ([MEDC][8]) MEDC's annual Renaissance Zone report confirms most state and local taxes, including real and personal property tax, are abated for specified years; it also confirms Corporate Income Tax, federal taxes, local bond obligations, school sinking fund, special assessments, and sales/use tax limitations, and describes official MSF actions and company-specific RERZ designations. ([MEDC][9]) Michigan Treasury ESA guidance gives renaissance-zone ESA phaseout multipliers and instructs taxpayers to report full acquisition cost while the system calculates the reduction. ([Michigan.gov][10]) Michigan Public Act 474 official text confirms MSF recommendation, local consent, continuous geographic area, revocation risk, development-agreement requirements, and annual reporting conditions. ([Michigan Legislature][11])

rules.evidenceText: ORC 5751.03 imposes CAT at two and six-tenths mills per dollar on taxable gross receipts after subtracting the exclusion amount, applies the full exclusion to the first calendar-quarter return, and carries unused exclusion forward to later quarters in the same year. ([Ohio Laws][12]) ORC Chapter 5751 states that CAT is levied on each person with taxable gross receipts for the privilege of doing business in Ohio, provides quarterly filing mechanics, and requires the fourth-quarter return to adjust over- or under-reported receipts for the calendar year. ([Ohio Laws][13]) Ohio's official CAT information release states that the annual minimum tax is eliminated for periods beginning January 1, 2024, the exclusion is $3,000,000 in 2024 and $6,000,000 in 2025 and thereafter, the 0.26% rate is unchanged, annual filing is eliminated after the 2023 return, taxpayers at or below the threshold are not required to file, and combined/consolidated groups are treated as one taxpayer. ([Cloudinary][14]) Ohio's official update for Q2 2025 confirms the $6,000,000-or-less cancellation message and electronic filing/payment routing through the Ohio Business Gateway. ([GovDelivery][15])
rules.reasoningNotes: Promote the current CAT constants and mechanics, but keep runtime status as needs_tax_return because a customer-facing amount requires the taxpayer's current return period, Ohio taxable gross receipts, group status, used exclusion, and account/filing status.
